notes: This batch covers the 19 required_core/compatibility_adapter 'inference/' rows
left unbound after wave-2 (CI-ROUTE-001..004 and CI-ROUTE-034 bound previously).
Ground truth for R's method-dispatch behaviour was read directly from the
pinned R/z-confint-gllvmTMB.R source (source_pins below), not from the
case-plan's templated per-row rationale strings, which repeat boilerplate
language across all CI-ROUTE-* rows and are not individually reliable for
the exact abort/withdrawal semantics per estimand.
R ground truth (confint.gllvmTMB_multi + its .confint_icc / .confint_phylo_signal
/ .confint_communality / .confint_rho / .confint_proportion internal helpers):
each of icc/phylo_signal/communality/rho/proportion routes on `parm` BEFORE the
outer confint.gllvmTMB_multi match.arg(method), then validates `method` itself
with a `switch(method, ..., cli::cli_abort(...))` or `if/else-if/else` whose
reject branch fires for any method string outside that estimand's own supported
set -- and, critically, NEVER touches the fit-structure-dependent estimator
function (extract_repeatability / .communality_wald_ci / extract_correlations /
.proportions_wald_ci / profile_ci_phylo_signal / ...): parm-token parsing
(.parse_communality_parm / .parse_rho_parm / .parse_proportion_parm /
.parse_pertrait_parm) validates the tier NAME against a fixed string vocabulary
only, never against what the fit actually contains, so all 5 REJECT cases below
are safe to exercise on the cheap single-tier Gaussian fixture -- verified by
reading each dispatcher's branch order directly (see per-case r_call).
REPAIR (2026-09-01, after a Totoro run failure -- see git history / after-task
log for the incident): CORE070-INFERENCE-ICC-CI-METHOD-ROUTE (CI-ROUTE-008..011)
was originally listed as executable, computing icc via GLLVM's ordinary
GllvmFit + _make_communality_closure route against R's confint(parm='icc',
method='wald'/'bootstrap'). That crashed on Totoro: R's .confint_icc's wald/
bootstrap branches call extract_repeatability(), which requires vB > 0 AND
vW > 0 -- i.e. a genuine TWO-TIER fit (R: value ~ 0 + trait + latent(0 + trait
| site, d=1) + latent(0 + trait | site_species, d=1), matching
.unlazy/core070-aghq/oracle-source/readback/R/extract-repeatability.R's own
@examples block), and aborts on a single-tier fixture with 'Wald repeatability
needs vB > 0 and vW > 0; refit with ordinary latent or standalone indep at
each tier.' Building the matching Julia comparand is a DEEPER gap than a
fixture swap, though: docs/dev-log/core070/namespace-1-batch-contract.json
maps R's extract_repeatability -- not extract_ICC_site -- to Julia's
repeatability(fit::TwoLevelFit) in src/twolevel.jl (via fit_twolevel_gaussian),
a wholly separate struct from GllvmFit (grep confirms no confint*.jl file
references TwoLevelFit at all, and icc_wald_ci's signature is pinned to
::GllvmFit, so it cannot dispatch on a TwoLevelFit). repeatability(fit) returns
ONLY a point estimate -- src/twolevel.jl has zero Wald/profile/bootstrap CI
machinery for the two-level repeatability/ICC estimand (fit_twolevel_gaussian
itself does not even retain a Hessian/vcov). So a two-tier fixture on both
sides would still have no Julia CI function to call; the case has been moved
to needs_new_julia_surface (source_ids 008-011, case_id unchanged) rather than
kept executable against a wrong estimand (communality on a single-tier fit is
NOT the same quantity as vB/(vB+vW) repeatability on a two-tier fit) or forced
onto a fixture the target Julia function cannot consume.
icc's own supported set for the (still-reject-only) row cluster 012-014 is
{wald, bootstrap} -- method='profile' is NOT merely unsupported, it is a
separate explicit withdrawn-feature abort ('gllvmTMB_repeatability_profile_
withdrawn'); irrelevant to 012-014 since none of wald_asym/fisher-z/bogus is
'profile', but recorded for completeness given the needs_new_julia_surface note
above already touches extract_repeatability.
rho's own supported set is {fisher-z, wald, bootstrap} -- fisher-z is a VALID
rho method in R (already bound as CI-ROUTE-034/CORE070-INFERENCE-RHO-CI-METHOD-ROUTE
in wave2); this batch's rho reject case therefore covers only wald_asym (033) and
bogus (035), not fisher-z.
GLLVM.jl has no unified string/Symbol `method=` dispatcher for the derived-quantity
CIs (icc/phylo_signal/communality/rho/proportion): each method is a distinct
function (icc_wald_ci, profile_ci_derived, bootstrap_ci_derived, ... none of which
declare a `method` keyword). The Julia-side reject check therefore calls the
relevant existing Wald-CI function with an extraneous `method=<bad>` keyword and
asserts a MethodError is thrown -- a structurally different but equally loud
rejection mechanism (no such dispatch key exists at all, vs R's validated switch
default), documented explicitly rather than papered over.

cases.r_call: confint.gllvmTMB_multi(object, parm='icc', method=<'wald_asym'|'fisher-z'|'bogus'>) -> .confint_icc(method=...) -> if/else-if/else default branch -> cli_abort('Method ... not supported for icc. Available: wald, bootstrap.'). The default branch is reached WITHOUT ever calling extract_repeatability(), so this reject path needs no two-tier (vB>0, vW>0) fit -- confirmed by reading .confint_icc's branch order directly (only the wald/bootstrap branch calls extract_repeatability).
cases.julia_surface: icc_wald_ci(fit, f; method=<bad>) -- icc_wald_ci declares no `method` keyword, so any of the three bad values raises MethodError at the call site
cases.check: for each of the 3 bad method strings: R raises an error whose message contains 'not supported' and 'icc'; Julia raises MethodError
cases.fixture: shared single-tier Gaussian fixture (p=5, K=2, n=80, unit=site, gaussian(), n_init=1, se=TRUE), same convention as tools/core070_namespace_2_batch.R's oracle_g -- safe for this reject-only path (see r_call)

cases.r_call: confint.gllvmTMB_multi(object, parm='phylo_signal', method=<'wald_asym'|'fisher-z'|'bogus'>) -> .confint_phylo_signal(method=...) -> switch() default -> cli_abort('Method ... not implemented for phylo_signal. Available: profile, wald, bootstrap.'). switch() evaluates only the matched branch, so the default fires without calling profile_ci_phylo_signal / .phylo_signal_wald_ci / .phylo_signal_bootstrap_ci -- no phylogenetic block needed on the fit.
cases.julia_surface: phylo_signal_wald_ci(fit, t; method=<bad>) -- declares no `method` keyword, raises MethodError
cases.check: for each of the 3 bad method strings: R raises an error whose message contains 'not implemented' and 'phylo_signal'; Julia raises MethodError
cases.fixture: shared single-tier Gaussian fixture (no phylogenetic block needed -- the method switch fires before any phylo-specific computation)

Available: wald, bootstrap.'). .parse_communality_parm validates tier='unit' against a fixed string vocabulary only (no check against the fit's actual structure), and the method switch's default branch never calls .communality_wald_ci / .communality_bootstrap_ci.
cases.julia_surface: communality_wald_ci(fit, t; method=<bad>) -- declares no `method` keyword, raises MethodError
cases.check: for each of the 3 bad method strings: R raises an error whose message contains 'not implemented' and 'communality'; Julia raises MethodError

cases.r_call: confint.gllvmTMB_multi(object, parm='rho:unit:1,2', method=<'wald_asym'|'bogus'>) -> .confint_rho(method=...) -> else-branch -> cli_abort('Method ... not supported for rho. Available: fisher-z, wald, bootstrap.'). tier='unit' avoids the separate unit_slope/cluster/cluster2 early-abort branches; .parse_rho_parm validates the tier string only, and the method else-branch never calls extract_correlations. NOTE: fisher-z IS a valid rho method in R (CI-ROUTE-034, bound in wave2 as CORE070-INFERENCE-RHO-CI-METHOD-ROUTE); this case therefore covers only wald_asym and bogus, not fisher-z.

cases.check: for each of the 2 bad method strings: R raises an error whose message contains 'not supported' and 'rho'; Julia raises MethodError

cases.r_call: confint.gllvmTMB_multi(object, parm='proportion:shared_unit', method=<'wald_asym'|'fisher-z'|'bogus'>) -> .confint_proportion(method=...) -> switch() default -> cli_abort('Method ... not implemented for proportion. Available: wald, bootstrap.'). .parse_proportion_parm validates the component name ('shared_unit') against a fixed vocabulary only; the method switch's default branch never calls .proportions_wald_ci / .proportions_bootstrap_ci.
cases.julia_surface: icc_wald_ci(fit, f; method=<bad>) where f = GLLVM._make_communality_closure(spec, t) [proportion:shared_unit == the :shared component == communality convention, per confint_derived.jl's proportions() docstring: ':shared (== communality)'] -- declares no `method` keyword, raises MethodError
cases.check: for each of the 3 bad method strings: R raises an error whose message contains 'not implemented' and 'proportion'; Julia raises MethodError

needs_new_julia_surface.missing_surface: A standardized-loading/rho Wald CI analogous to R's loading_ci(method='wald_asym', loading_scale='standardized') with 'rho[trait,axis]' parameter naming
needs_new_julia_surface.reason: GLLVM.jl's confint(fit, y; parm='Lambda', method=:wald) computes the RAW-scale loading Wald CI (matching R's method='wald' branch, already bound as CI-ROUTE-003). R's method='wald_asym' is a DISTINCT route: it standardizes each loading to a [-1,1] correlation-like quantity and applies the Fisher-z transform before back-transforming, renaming parameters to rho[trait,axis]. No such standardized-loading closure or entry point exists yet in src/confint.jl or src/confint_derived_wald.jl; the closest building block is the existing Fisher-z machinery (_tw_link(:fisher_z) / _tw_fisher_z / _tw_fisher_z_inv in src/confint_derived_wald.jl) applied to a per-entry closure that does not yet exist. Building it is new src/ engineering (a new public CI function plus a standardized-loading packed-theta closure), out of scope for this coverage batch; recorded here as BLOCKED pending that surface, not fudged as a raw-scale wald pass under a different name.

needs_new_julia_surface.missing_surface: A Wald/profile/bootstrap confidence interval for the two-level repeatability/ICC estimand R_t = vB[t] / (vB[t] + vW[t]) on GLLVM.jl's TwoLevelFit
needs_new_julia_surface.reason: R's confint(parm='icc', method='wald'/'bootstrap') routes through extract_repeatability(), which requires a genuine TWO-TIER fit (vB>0 from a between/unit-level latent block AND vW>0 from a within/observation-level latent block -- R construction: value ~ 0 + trait + latent(0 + trait | site, d=1) + latent(0 + trait | site_species, d=1), per .unlazy/core070-aghq/oracle-source/readback/R/extract-repeatability.R's own @examples). GLLVM.jl's analogous struct is TwoLevelFit / fit_twolevel_gaussian in src/twolevel.jl (this mapping is itself pinned in docs/dev-log/core070/namespace-1-batch-contract.json: extract_repeatability -> repeatability(fit::TwoLevelFit) src/twolevel.jl:263, NOT icc_wald_ci -- the case-plan's julia_surface text pointing at icc_wald_ci for this row was a misidentification, confirmed wrong by a Totoro run failure in .confint_icc/extract_repeatability's vB/vW guard on a single-tier fixture). repeatability(fit::TwoLevelFit) returns ONLY a bare point estimate: src/twolevel.jl has no Wald, profile, or bootstrap CI machinery for it at all (grep across src/*.jl confirms no confint*.jl file references TwoLevelFit; fit_twolevel_gaussian's Optim.LBFGS fit does not even retain a Hessian/vcov to build one from), and icc_wald_ci's signature is pinned to ::GllvmFit so it cannot dispatch on a TwoLevelFit regardless. Fitting a matched two-tier model on both sides would therefore still leave nothing to call on the Julia side; recorded here as BLOCKED pending that CI surface, not forced onto the wrong estimand (single-tier communality) or a fixture the target function cannot consume.
